problem: Existing world action models (WAMs) built for stationary manipulation mismatch mobile manipulation in three ways: coarse chunk-level video latents vs. per-step control, one entangled action space for base and arm, and training on ground-truth or arbitrarily noised futures vs. self-predicted futures at inference.
motivation: Mobile manipulation needs long-horizon context, large viewpoint changes and precise contact-level control, so small prediction errors compound over long rollouts. The authors argue the bottleneck is structural alignment of world modeling, action abstraction and rollout conditioning, not just scale.
key_idea: Cascade video latent -> frame-level latent action -> executable action inside a Wan2.2-based dual-level Mixture-of-Transformers with separate base/arm action towers, and train the action head on the model's own dreamed futures (Dream Forcing).
insight: Each alignment component gives a measurable gain in the ablations. On RoboTwin clean, a 3-stage latent-action design with no conditioning dropout reaches 94.00 vs. 87.60 for direct video-to-action, and dropping latent actions with p=0.2 hurts (91.06) because of a train-test mismatch. Dream Forcing from a 50k-step checkpoint gives 70.56 after 5k steps, while continued teacher forcing gives 66.78 (5k) and 68.90 (10k). Large-scale pretraining matters most in low-data settings: 49.0 vs. 17.8 for plain Wan2.2 fine-tuning at Target 10%.
method: Latent action cascade: a frozen ALAM-pretrained encoder E_m(I_t,I_t+1) gives frame-level latent actions (H x N_c x d_m); the model generates z_{t+1} -> m_t -> a_t with asymmetric attention (video tokens cannot see latent-action tokens; action tokens see them).

Dual-level MoT: modality-level experts (separate input projections, timestep embeddings and heads for video, latent action and action) plus action-level sub-towers (own FFN and head) for base mobility vs. arm manipulation, with joint self-attention across all tokens.

Subspace-aware CFM: flow matching for both action branches with one shared denoising timestep, each branch seeing the other's noisy action, weighted lambda_move/lambda_manip, teacher-forced upstream during SFT1.

Dream Forcing: two-phase forward pass where Phase A generates dreamed z_hat_{t+1}, m_hat_t for the latest chunk (few-step denoising, parallel, Self-Forcing style) and Phase B predicts actions conditioned on them.

Training pipeline: Wan2.2-5B world-model pretraining on OXE, OXE-AugE, Agibot-Beta, RoboCOIN, RoboMind, Galaxea, InternData-A1, RoboNet, BridgeData V2 and DROID with 4 fixed camera semantic slots; ALAM latent action pretraining; SFT1 (GT-conditioned), SFT2 (Dream Forcing).

Systems tricks: structured sparse attention rewritten as varlen FlashAttention (~5x fwd+bwd speedup over FlexAttention), and offset-based latent augmentation (H starting offsets) for precomputed video latents.

setting.backbone: Wan2.2-5B video diffusion backbone with dual-level MoT (video, latent action, mobility action, manipulation action experts), fine-tuned end-to-end
setting.training_data: Large-scale public and synthetic robot data (OXE, OXE-AugE, Agibot-Beta, RoboCOIN, RoboMind, Galaxea, InternData-A1, RoboNet, BridgeData V2, DROID) for pretraining, then benchmark-specific SFT; 50 demos per real-world task
setting.observation: multi-view RGB (up to 4 slots: 2 third-person, 2 wrist) plus language instruction
setting.action_space: low-level continuous robot actions (mobility + manipulation) predicted as chunks via flow matching
setting.simulator: RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO / LIBERO-Plus; real Agilex Piper arm

numbers_note: Real-world results are given mainly in a figure. Text gives Peg Cylinder 70% SR / 96% process score, and Organize Plate 70%, Arrange Fruits 80%, Cup Stacking 80%, Arrange Flower 60%. No navigation-benchmark numbers (R2R, ObjectNav, etc.). It is a mobile-manipulation paper.
results: ABot-M0.5 reaches 54.2% average on RoboCasa365 Target 100%, above Lingbot-VA (45.1), GR00T-N1.5 (43.7) and Fast-WAM (43.5). It also reaches 94.10 on RoboTwin 2.0 (vs. Qwen-RobotManip 93.85), 99.4 on LIBERO and 83.4 total on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus (best among WAMs). With condensed memory, the pretrained model reaches 46.6% average on RoboCasa365 vs. Qwen-RobotManip's 35.9%. Composite-Unseen is weaker at 2.7% (Qwen-RobotManip 14.9%).
limitations: Real-world evaluation is only a single fixed 6-DoF Agilex Piper arm with 5 tasks and 50 demos each, without an actual mobile base; the ablations are small and single-benchmark.
Weak generalization to unseen compositions in the pretraining setting (Composite-Unseen 2.7%), and LIBERO-Plus robustness is uneven (Noise 75.5, Camera 70.5).
Inference latency and cost of the 5B video-diffusion model are not reported; the condensed-memory extension is undescribed.
